question: On a pull request's head: after a push, is every required check pending again; does a required check conclude `timed_out`, `neutral`, `skipped`, `cancelled` or `stale` and keep that conclusion until the content changes or a person runs it again; is every check run read with its exact name and its App's id, two workflow runs on one commit both staying, since `filter=latest` is per check suite; and can any App with `checks: write`, or any Actions job, post a check run under a required Lens's check name, or a result for any criterion of a contract, one the contract does not name among them, which then stays on that head?
pass: Written 2026-10-22T18:07:40Z, before the window: after a push the new head's required check is pending; timed_out, neutral, skipped and cancelled conclusions keep an hour apart; each check run has its name and App id; two runs on one commit both stay; the pr-review App and an Actions job post under a required check's name and an unlisted criterion's, and both stay. On canary pull request 65, the trial-author App's, p42-checks.yml ran on pull_request and on push: two suites on one commit. The Maintainer cancelled the pull_request run at 02:20:29Z (gh run cancel, which prints nothing). Failed as written: no check concluded timed_out. The job p42 / timed-out, held to timeout-minutes: 1, was stopped at its limit in the push run, which no one cancelled, and GitHub concluded the job, its check run and the run cancelled, its annotation saying the job exceeded its maximum execution time. The rest holds: neutral, skipped and cancelled conclusions are unchanged an hour after the last post; each check run carries its name and its App's id; filter=latest keeps one run of a name in each suite, and filter=all every run; the pr-review App (5364144) and an Actions job (15368) each posted p2-queue-check and an unlisted criterion's result, and all stayed; after the App's push the new head's p2-queue-check was in progress. The pr-review App's first two posts took the repo's name by a script's bug, and stay on the head too.
